blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Find the global and local extrema of \(f(x) = 4 - x^{2}\) over \([-1, 2]\). (Hint: Use the increasing and decreasing behavior of the functions including the end points.)
blocks.explanation:
Global and local extrema on a closed interval, end points included.
Given \(f(x) = 4 - x^{2}\) on \([-1, 2]\).
Plan: sign table of \(f'\), values at the critical point and the end points, then read local extrema from the rise and fall (as in Figure 2.5) and global ones by comparing.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 4 - x^{2}\), \(x \in [-1, 2]\).
To find: all local extrema and the global extrema.
Method: increasing/decreasing behaviour (2.9.2) plus the values (2.10.3). An end point is a local maximum if \(f\) falls away from it into the interval, a local minimum if \(f\) rises away from it.

Critical point
\[f'(x) = -2x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0 \in [-1, 2]\]
Why: \(f'\) exists everywhere.

Sign of \(f'\)
\[f'\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) = 1 > 0 \text{ on } (-1, 0)\]
\[f'(1) = -2 < 0 \text{ on } (0, 2)\]
Why: increasing on \([-1, 0]\), decreasing on \([0, 2]\).

Values
\[f(-1) = 3,\quad f(0) = 4,\quad f(2) = 0\]
Why: the critical point and both end points.

Local extrema
\(x = 0\): increasing then decreasing: local maximum \(f(0) = 4\).
\(x = -1\) (left end): \(f\) increases just after it: local minimum \(f(-1) = 3\).
\(x = 2\) (right end): \(f\) decreases up to it: local minimum \(f(2) = 0\).
Why: the definitions of 2.10.2 use \(I \cap I_{1}\), so an end point is compared only with the points of the interval next to it.

Global extrema
Comparing 3, 4, 0: global maximum 4, global minimum 0.
Why: 2.10.3.
Check: \(4 - x^{2} \le 4\) always, and on \([-1, 2]\) the largest \(x^{2}\) is \(2^{2} = 4\), giving the least value 0.
blocks.final_answer: Local maximum \(f(0) = 4\) (also the global maximum); local minima \(f(-1) = 3\) and \(f(2) = 0\); the global minimum is \(f(2) = 0\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) Find the global and local extrema of \(f(x) = \cos x - \sin x\) over \([0, 2\pi]\). (Hint: Use the increasing and decreasing behavior of the functions including the end points.)
blocks.explanation:
Global and local extrema of a trigonometric function on \([0, 2\pi]\).
Given \(f(x) = \cos x - \sin x\).
Plan: critical points from \(\tan x = -1\), sign table, values, then local and global extrema including the end points.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \cos x - \sin x\), \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
To find: all local extrema and the global extrema.
Method: increasing/decreasing behaviour and values, as in part (i).

Critical points
\[f'(x) = -\sin x - \cos x = 0\]
\[\tan x = -1\]
\[x = \dfrac{3\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\]
Why: \(\sin x = -\cos x\); tangent is negative in quadrants II and IV: \(\pi - \frac{\pi}{4}\) and \(2\pi - \frac{\pi}{4}\).

Sign of \(f'\)
\[f'\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = -1 < 0 \text{ on } \left(0, \tfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)\]
\[f'(\pi) = 1 > 0 \text{ on } \left(\tfrac{3\pi}{4}, \tfrac{7\pi}{4}\right)\]
\[f'\left(\tfrac{11\pi}{6}\right) = \tfrac{1 - \sqrt{3}}{2} < 0 \text{ on } \left(\tfrac{7\pi}{4}, 2\pi\right)\]
Why: \(f'\left(\frac{11\pi}{6}\right) = -\left(-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\).

Local extrema
\(x = 0\) (left end): \(f\) decreases just after it: local maximum \(f(0) = 1\).
\(x = \frac{3\pi}{4}\): decreasing then increasing: local minimum \(-\sqrt{2}\).
\(x = \frac{7\pi}{4}\): increasing then decreasing: local maximum \(\sqrt{2}\).
\(x = 2\pi\) (right end): \(f\) decreases up to it: local minimum \(f(2\pi) = 1\).
Why: read from the sign table, end points included.

Global extrema
Comparing \(1, -\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2}, 1\): global maximum \(\sqrt{2}\), global minimum \(-\sqrt{2}\).
Why: 2.10.3.
Check: \(\cos x - \sin x = \sqrt{2}\cos\left(x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) lies between \(-\sqrt{2}\) and \(\sqrt{2}\).
blocks.final_answer: Local maxima \(f(0) = 1\) and \(f\left(\frac{7\pi}{4}\right) = \sqrt{2}\); local minima \(f\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right) = -\sqrt{2}\) and \(f(2\pi) = 1\). Global maximum value \(\sqrt{2}\) at \(x = \frac{7\pi}{4}\); global minimum value \(-\sqrt{2}\) at \(x = \frac{3\pi}{4}\).
